clue.text: Resin melted where very hot, splitting bag

indicators.note: one piece splits the bag word, opening it up to sit inside it

parts.note: a sac is a bag or pouch
hell, the inferno, is the place so hot that sinners would melt

explanation.surface: A resin melts in fierce heat and bursts through the bag holding it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'melted where very hot' reads like a description of the resin, but it clues the place of eternal fire; 'splitting' puts that inside the bag word.
explanation.definitionFit: Shellac is a natural resin secreted by the lac insect, used in varnish.

clue.text: Point aligns, going off the rails

indicators.note: something going off the rails runs out of control, so these letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A railway point lines up, then the train derails.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going off the rails' rearranges ALIGNS. 'Point' looks like a railway point but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To point at something is to indicate it, to give a sign.

clue.text: Bond blows top about joke apparatus

indicators.note: the trimmed bond word goes around the joke word, about meaning surrounding
losing its top removes the first letter of the bond word

parts.note: cement is a bond, a binding material
a quip is a witty joke

explanation.surface: Someone loses their temper over a gag about a piece of kit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blows top' strips C from CEMENT to leave EMENT, which goes 'about' QUIP. 'Bond' tempts as James Bond.
explanation.definitionFit: Equipment is the gear or apparatus needed for a job.

clue.text: Jail ultimately providing Her Majesty with its permanent resident?

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the word jail

parts.note: providing means if, on condition that
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the abbreviation for the Queen

explanation.surface: A prison and the Queen are linked to a long-term inmate.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the playful definition: a prisoner serving life is a jail's permanent resident.
explanation.definitionFit: A lifer is a prisoner serving a life sentence, who may never leave.

clue.text: Blooming people who drive?

parts.note: read as a whole population of motorists, a ..., which also names a flower in bloom

explanation.definitionFit: A carnation is a garden flower, and split in two it reads as a country of motorists.

clue.text: Time to go back into perfect part of mosque

indicators.note: into places the turned time word inside the perfect word

parts.note: in mint condition means perfect, as new

indicators.note: going back means the time word is read from right to left

parts.note: an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: A moment for restoring part of a mosque to pristine state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to go back' turns ERA into ARE, which goes 'into' MINT.
explanation.definitionFit: A minaret is the slender tower of a mosque from which the call to prayer is made.

clue.text: Appeared low in vehicle

explanation.definitionFit: To mope is to look gloomy, so moped means appeared down; it is also a small motorbike.

clue.text: Social activities approaching, I felt excited

parts.note: nigh means near, approaching

indicators.note: excited letters are stirred up into a different arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone feels thrilled as a party draws near.
explanation.walkthrough: 'excited' rearranges I FELT; 'approaching' is the adjective near, not the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Nightlife is the entertainment and socialising available in the evening.

clue.text: Criticise traditional dinner

explanation.definitionFit: To roast someone is to criticise harshly; a roast is the classic Sunday meal of cooked meat.

clue.text: Utterly stupid to accept first of applicants as guardian

indicators.note: accepting means taking in, so the scrambled word holds the extra letter
stupid suggests the letters are muddled and senseless
first of picks the opening letter of applicants

explanation.surface: Someone thinks it daft to take on applicants as guardians.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stupid' rearranges UTTERLY, which 'to accept' takes in A from applicants. 'as' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Tutelary means acting as protector or guardian, as in a tutelary deity.

clue.text: Coarse frill put on back of ribbing

indicators.note: put on means the frill word is attached next to the selected letter
back of picks the final letter of the word ribbing

parts.note: a ruff is a frilled collar

explanation.surface: A rough frill is sewn on behind some ribbed knitwear.
explanation.walkthrough: G, the last letter of 'ribbing', comes first, with RUFF 'put on' it.
explanation.definitionFit: Gruff means rough and harsh in manner or voice.

clue.text: Ruling about backing up? Foul!

indicators.note: the ruling word goes about, around, the turned word

parts.note: regnant means reigning, ruling

indicators.note: backing means the word up is reversed

explanation.surface: A referee's decision about a backward pass draws a cry of foul.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' turns UP into PU, and REGNANT goes 'about' it.
explanation.definitionFit: Repugnant means disgusting, offensive, vile.

clue.text: Sign 'inders what it stands for

parts.note: hinders means hampers, and the dropped H shown by the apostrophe drops it again
the sign in question means and

explanation.surface: A cockney asks what a sign that gets in the way stands for.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in ''inders' shows a dropped H, so the synonym HAMPERS loses its H too. The ampersand is the sign &, standing for 'and'.
explanation.definitionFit: An ampersand is the printed symbol & used for the word and.

clue.text: Sum-little one plus two-thirds of everything

parts.note: a tot is a small child

indicators.note: two-thirds keeps two of the three letters of the everything word

parts.note: all means everything

explanation.surface: Arithmetic for a child: one plus most of everything.
explanation.walkthrough: The dash in 'Sum-little' separates the definition from the wordplay; 'plus' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A total is the full amount obtained by adding things up.

clue.text: Bring up opinion by newspaper which offers reflection

parts.note: to rear a child is to bring it up
a view is an opinion
the Mirror is a British daily tabloid newspaper

explanation.surface: Raising one's opinion via the press, which prompts thought.
explanation.walkthrough: The Mirror is a British tabloid. 'reflection' looks like pondering but is literal: the car mirror reflects the road behind.
explanation.definitionFit: A rear-view mirror shows the driver a reflected image of traffic behind.

clue.text: Executed choice remark

indicators.note: executed means beheaded, so the choice word loses its head, its first letter

parts.note: a preference is a choice

explanation.surface: A choice comment about carrying out a sentence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Executed' beheads PREFERENCE, removing P. It looks like 'carried out' in the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A reference is a mention or allusion made in passing, a remark.

clue.text: Is deception an offence under western state?

indicators.note: in a down clue, the pieces placed under a letter come after it

parts.note: a con is a deception, a swindle
a sin is an offence or wrongdoing

explanation.surface: A question of whether trickery counts as a crime in Western law.
explanation.walkthrough: 'under' puts IS CON SIN beneath W in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Wisconsin is one of the US states, in the Midwest.

clue.text: One trail, a ridiculous theory

indicators.note: ridiculous suggests the letters are absurdly jumbled up

explanation.surface: One far-fetched lead offered as an explanation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ridiculous' rearranges ONE TRAIL A.
explanation.definitionFit: A rationale is the reasoning or explanation behind something.

clue.text: Massive bereavement in the mining industry

indicators.note: in places the bereavement word inside the mining word

parts.note: coal stands for the mining industry, as in coal-mining
a bereavement is a loss through death

explanation.surface: A huge loss of life in a mining disaster.
explanation.walkthrough: LOSS goes 'in' COAL, giving CO-LOSS-AL.
explanation.definitionFit: Colossal means enormous, immense, huge.

clue.text: Unable to cope, so going under?

explanation.definitionFit: Being beyond one's ability is idiomatically being in water too deep, and a swimmer in such water would sink.

clue.text: French distanced from outburst, yours truly providing catalyst

indicators.note: distanced from means the French abbreviation is taken away from the outburst word

parts.note: a frenzy is a wild outburst
yours truly means the speaker, me

explanation.surface: A Frenchman calms down from a tantrum, and the speaker sparks a reaction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'distanced from' removes FR from FRENZY to leave ENZY, then add ME. 'providing' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An enzyme is a protein that speeds up a biological reaction, a biological catalyst.

clue.text: Ruling brothers

explanation.definitionFit: An order is a command or ruling, and also a religious community of monks or friars.

clue.text: Sketch what one may wish to exclude, say

indicators.note: say signals that the word is to be spoken, not spelt

parts.words: what one may wish to exclude
parts.note: a draught is a cold current of air one keeps out with a door seal

explanation.surface: A sketch of something one would rather leave out.
explanation.walkthrough: DRAUGHT, a cold breeze, is a British spelling pronounced like DRAFT.
explanation.definitionFit: A draft is a preliminary version or outline, a sketch.

clue.text: Farm animal has no wool, God admitted

indicators.note: admitted means let in, so the god sits inside the sheared word

parts.note: a sheep that is shorn has had its wool cut off
Thor is the Norse god of thunder

explanation.surface: A sheared farm animal is let in by a deity.
explanation.walkthrough: THOR is 'admitted' into SHORN.
explanation.definitionFit: The Shorthorn is a breed of cattle.

clue.text: Run-down clock, time emptied

parts.note: to clock is slang for to see or notice

indicators.note: emptied removes the inside, leaving only the first and last letters of the time word

parts.note: a day is a period of time

explanation.surface: A clock has wound down and stopped telling the time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clock' is the slang verb meaning notice. 'emptied' strips the middle A from DAY.
explanation.definitionFit: Seedy means shabby, squalid, dilapidated.

clue.text: Said to be finished with cast

indicators.note: said to be signals that the word is spoken, a sound-alike

parts.note: to be through is to be finished

explanation.surface: An actor reportedly done with the rest of the cast.
explanation.walkthrough: THROUGH, finished, sounds like THREW. 'cast' looks like actors but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Threw is the past tense of throw, which is what cast means as a verb.

clue.text: Saltiness at sea won't rust

indicators.note: at sea means confused, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Salt water at sea, yet the metal won't corrode.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at sea' rearranges SALTINESS.
explanation.definitionFit: Stainless steel resists corrosion, so it will not rust.

clue.text: US major in army finally prepared

parts.note: in America to major in a subject is to read it at university

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of the word army

explanation.surface: An American officer in the army is finally ready.
explanation.walkthrough: 'US major in' is not an officer: to major in a subject at a US college is to READ it, in British terms.
explanation.definitionFit: Ready means prepared, all set.

clue.text: Swimmer breaking limits of lucky game of chance

indicators.note: breaking means the swimmer forces its way in between the limits
limits of picks the first and last letters of lucky

parts.note: an otter is a swimming mammal

explanation.surface: A swimmer bursts through the edges of a lucky game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'limits of' gives L and Y, and OTTER is 'breaking' them apart.
explanation.definitionFit: A lottery is a draw in which prizes go to random tickets.

clue.text: Nonexistent place — then there is the opposite?

parts.note: the opposite of then, the past, is now
the opposite of there is here

explanation.surface: A place that does not exist, followed by a quibble about opposites.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is the opposite' tells the solver to swap each of 'then' and 'there' for its opposite.
explanation.definitionFit: Nowhere means no place at all, a place that does not exist.
